Starbucks (SBUX) Stock Could Be 33% Overvalued As Growth Plans Expand
sum: Starbucks shares have climbed 27.2% over the past year, and with investors focused on expansion plans and profitability, the real issue is whether the current price is supported by the cash the business is expected to generate. The stock now trades around US$106, so the key lens is what its cash flows suggest about intrinsic value.
The 27.2% 1 year return puts real weight on the question of whether Starbucks' current valuation can be explained by its cash flow profile.
Management is leaning into global store growth and digital investments, which can reshape both the timing and level of future cash inflows as new locations and higher service efficiency reach scale.
For investors, the debate is whether Starbucks' recent share price strength is adequately backed by the cash flows implied by a Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) view of its intrinsic value.
To pressure test Starbucks' 27.2% 1 year return against similar cash flow stories, it helps to weigh it against other companies screened for 42 high quality undervalued stocks

The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model here uses Starbucks' projected free cash flows to judge what the current price implies. Latest twelve month free cash flow sits at about $2.8b, with the model assuming that this builds over time into higher annual cash generation by the late 2020s and early 2030s rather than shrinking.

On those cash flow forecasts, the DCF suggests an estimated intrinsic value that is substantially below the present share price of $106.16. Starbucks' push to add thousands of new outlets and sharpen digital ordering, highlighted in the recent "Back to Starbucks" growth plan, helps explain why the market is willing to pay a richer price than the cash flow model supports right now. NVDA Stock In For ‘Very, Very Fast’ Rally: Analysts Shrug Off Price-Hike Buzz Ahead Of Most-Watched Earnings Report
sum: Shares of Nvidia, Inc. (NVDA) rose nearly 1% in premarket trading on Tuesday, attempting to rebound from a seven-session rout as analysts argued that potential price increases for its newest AI systems should not derail demand and could strengthen an already bullish earnings setup.
NVDA stock fell 3% on Monday but remains up 4% for August, putting it on track for its strongest monthly performance since May.

Nvidia could reportedly raise prices for its Blackwell and Rubin systems as soaring memory costs push up production expenses. However, Raymond James analyst Simon Leopold said that a potential 15% increase would make sense given the amount of high-bandwidth memory packed into the platforms. “15% really doesn’t seem all that demanding,” Leopold said, adding that an even larger increase is possible.

Each Blackwell and Rubin GPU is paired with eight HBM stacks, each containing 12 layers of DRAM. Nvidia has also spent years locking in memory supplies through long-term agreements with multiple suppliers, potentially cushioning the effect of rising costs.

Still, Leopold cautioned that higher list prices may not translate directly into higher prices for major customers. “The public prices may go up by 15%, but that doesn’t mean contracted prices are reflecting that same amount,” he said.

Wall Street is bracing for another enormous quarter from Nvidia on Wednesday. Fiscal.ai projects revenue of $91.48 billion, more than double the year-earlier figure, with adjusted earnings of $2.07 per share and EBITDA of $61.83 billion.

Koyfin’s estimates are slightly higher at $92.07 billion in revenue, $2.09 in adjusted earnings and $61.99 billion in EBITDA. This would represent sequential growth of 13% in revenue and EBITDA and 12% in earnings.

McDonald's Stock Down 23% in 6 Months: Should Investors Buy the Dip?
sum: McDonald's Corporation’s MCD shares have declined 22.9% over the past six months, underperforming the restaurant industry, which fell 16.7%, and the S&P 500, which gained 10.8%. The sell-off reflects concerns about slowing U.S. sales momentum, inconsistent execution of value offerings, weaker-than-expected marketing results and a challenging consumer environment.

McDonald's stock has faced several headwinds over the past six months. First, the U.S. business has struggled to generate stronger comparable sales growth amid a challenging consumer environment. Second, the company's value-menu strategy did not deliver the expected increase in customer traffic. Third, operational inefficiencies and underwhelming marketing campaigns weakened customer engagement. Concerns about development costs and a slower restaurant expansion timeline have added to the challenges.

These issues were evident in the second quarter of 2026, when global comparable sales increased just 1.3%, while U.S. comparable sales grew 0.8%. Management acknowledged that execution in the United States fell short of expectations.
In the same time frame, McDonald’s has underperformed restaurant peers including Starbucks Corporation SBUX, Yum! Brands, Inc. YUM and Chipotle Mexican Grill, Inc. CMG.

McDonald's introduced its Every Day Affordable Price menu in April 2026, offering 10 items priced below $3. However, the initiative failed to generate the expected incremental sales because of inconsistent execution and limited consumer awareness. Only about 60-65% of the U.S. restaurant system followed the recommended pricing structure.

The company also reduced digital offers and discontinued its Buy One, Add One for $1 promotion to offset the cost of its value initiatives. These changes disappointed some frequent customers. Management attributed roughly two-thirds of the U.S. customer traffic shortfall against its expectations to these value-related execution issues.

Marketing performance added to the pressure. McDonald's U.S. business faced a difficult comparison with the previous year's successful Minecraft campaign, while its FIFA campaign in June generated less business than expected. These shortcomings suggest that the company needs to improve its promotional strategy to bring customers back more consistently.
